description: AI-2 evaluation set (ai-assist.md §6): the error catalogue's worded refusals and the sample tenant's product premiums. Sample data only; the rates are invented.

refusals.means: Privileged access is granted for a limited time, and the period asked for is longer than allowed.
refusals.remedy: Ask for a shorter period.

refusals.means: The amount is above the limit of your approval authority.
refusals.remedy: Ask a colleague whose limit covers the amount to decide it.

refusals.means: None of your roles has approval authority for this type of approval.
refusals.remedy: Ask a colleague who has the authority to decide it, or ask your administrator about yours.

refusals.means: Only the person who asked for this approval can withdraw it.
refusals.remedy: Ask the requester to withdraw it, or let a checker decide it.

refusals.means: Each document needs your confirmation that it holds no customer personal data before AI-1 reads it.
refusals.remedy: Confirm each document, then start the run again.

refusals.means: A document's content changed after you confirmed it, so the run didn't read it.
refusals.remedy: Check the document again, then start a new run and confirm it again.

refusals.means: A document holds an obvious identifier, such as an email address, an ID number or a bank account number, so AI-1 refused it and sent nothing. The run lists the kind of identifier and the page.
refusals.remedy: Remove the identifiers from the document, upload the corrected copy, then start a new run.

refusals.means: A document isn't one AI-1 reads: a run takes 1 to 10 different documents, each a PDF, DOCX or XLSX file of at most 20 MB, filed under a category that holds no personal data.
refusals.remedy: Check the documents against those limits, then start the run again with documents that meet them.

refusals.means: Only the user who uploaded a document can confirm it holds no customer personal data, and someone else uploaded this one.
refusals.remedy: Upload the document again yourself, then start the run with your copy.

refusals.means: The approval was for different content from the version as it now stands.
refusals.remedy: Read the version again, check its review sheet, and approve the content it now has.

refusals.means: A regulated value can come only from an overlay version that has been approved for your tenant, and this one hasn't been.
refusals.remedy: Use an approved version, or ask for this one to be reviewed and approved.

refusals.means: Only a pack's newest version can be approved, so that a correction isn't overtaken by the version it corrects.
refusals.remedy: Approve the newest version, after reading its review sheet.

refusals.means: The region your settings name for AI inference isn't one the AI provider can run in, so no explanation is asked for.
refusals.remedy: Ask your administrator to choose one of the regions offered in the AI Assist settings, with the legal basis for it.

refusals.means: The AI provider said it answered from outside your tenant's inference region, so nothing it returned was used.
refusals.remedy: Start a new run later. If it happens again, ask your administrator to check the AI Assist settings.

refusals.means: The run waited more than an hour to start, so its confirmations are no longer relied on.
refusals.remedy: Start a new run and confirm the documents again.

refusals.means: A role that can start an AI product draft must also be able to review it.
refusals.remedy: Grant ASSIST_PRODUCT_DRAFT_REVIEW to the role first, or end ASSIST_PRODUCT_DRAFT_RUN before ending the review function.

refusals.means: The run was interrupted part way and isn't resumed.
refusals.remedy: Start a new run. If the run created a Draft version, finish that one first: a product has one version in progress at a time.

refusals.means: The setup changed while the AI pass ran: its answers changed or it was submitted, so nothing the pass found was recorded in it.
refusals.remedy: Read the setup again and ask for a new pass if it is still a draft.

refusals.means: The setup can't be submitted yet: a value is missing or undecided, a regulated value isn't from an overlay approved for your tenant, or a table refuses a value.
refusals.remedy: Read the setup's completeness check, correct each blocker it lists, and submit again.

refusals.means: An AI pass is already queued or running on this setup, and a setup takes one pass at a time.
refusals.remedy: Wait for the pass to finish, then read the setup again and ask for another if you need one.

refusals.means: The documents hold more than AI-1 reads in one run: a file that expands too far, a sheet that is too large, or too much text in total.
refusals.remedy: Split the material into smaller files, or start runs with fewer documents.

refusals.means: A document couldn't be read: the file couldn't be opened, or none of its pages has text, such as a scanned image.
refusals.remedy: Upload a copy with a text layer, for example the original file rather than a scan, then start a new run.

refusals.means: A tenant's own overlay is loaded only while the tenant is onboarding, and this one is live.
refusals.remedy: Use an overlay approved for every tenant, or change configuration through the normal change process.

refusals.means: The run stopped without writing anything, because you can no longer do what it does for you: your account or your roles changed after you started it.
refusals.remedy: Ask your administrator to check your access, then start a new run.

refusals.means: This callback was already received.
refusals.remedy: Nothing to do: the first one was recorded.

refusals.means: A provider's callback wasn't accepted, as its signature, key, timestamp or token isn't valid.
refusals.remedy: Check the provider's endpoint set-up with your integration administrator.

refusals.means: The channel requires an approval for this transaction, and the transaction has no approval step.
refusals.remedy: Make the transaction on a channel that doesn't require approval, or ask your administrator to change the channel's setting.

refusals.means: Your roles may not make this transaction, for this product, on this channel.
refusals.remedy: Ask your administrator whether the channel's permissions should allow it, or use another channel that does.

refusals.means: The application you're using isn't on a channel your organisation has enabled for this.
refusals.remedy: Use the application your organisation has enabled for it, or ask your administrator to enable the channel.

refusals.means: The claim's event date is after today's business date.
refusals.remedy: Correct the event date.

refusals.means: The carried amount has not been owed long enough to invoice, and the intermediary is not terminated.
refusals.remedy: Invoice it once it has been carried for the tenant's number of days (90 unless set in the commission settings), or once the intermediary is terminated.

refusals.means: Someone else changed the record at the same moment.
refusals.remedy: Try again; if it repeats, open the record again first.

refusals.means: The amounts are in different currencies, which this action doesn't allow.
refusals.remedy: Use amounts in the record's currency.

refusals.means: The service is too busy to take the request just now.
refusals.remedy: Try again shortly.

refusals.means: The change breaks a rule the records must always keep.
refusals.remedy: Check the values against the related records; if they look right, report it to support with the reference.

refusals.means: A mandatory notice hasn't been acknowledged at this point of the process.
refusals.remedy: Record the customer's acknowledgement of the notice, then try again.

refusals.means: The uploaded file is held until a malware scan clears it, or it failed the scan.
refusals.remedy: Wait for the scan, then open it again; a file that failed the scan has to be uploaded again from a clean copy.

refusals.means: The record doesn't pass the checks this step of the process requires.
refusals.remedy: Correct the record as the checks require, then try again.

refusals.means: The party hasn't been cleared by customer due diligence for this step, so INSYS won't go on with it.
refusals.remedy: Ask a compliance officer to complete the outstanding due diligence items for the party; the step can then be done.

refusals.means: A record with the same identifying values already exists.
refusals.remedy: Look for the existing record and work on it, or change the identifying values.

refusals.means: Portal users can use only their own portal's functions.
refusals.remedy: Use the portal for this, or contact the insurer.

refusals.means: Your organisation isn't entitled to the feature this action belongs to.
refusals.remedy: Ask your tenant administrator; the entitlement is set by the platform operator.

refusals.means: You aren't allowed to do this.
refusals.remedy: Ask your administrator whether your role should allow it.

refusals.means: This action is switched off for your organisation, or isn't available on the platform.
refusals.remedy: Ask your tenant administrator whether it should be switched on.

refusals.means: None of your roles in force grants this action.
refusals.remedy: Ask your tenant administrator for a role that includes it, or ask a colleague who holds it.

refusals.means: A change to how static data is approved is already waiting for a decision.
refusals.remedy: Wait for that decision before asking for another.

refusals.means: The same request is still being processed.
refusals.remedy: Wait a moment, then check the record before trying again.

refusals.means: The request was sent without the key that stops it being made twice.
refusals.remedy: Send it again from the application; this is a technical step it should add.

refusals.means: The request's key was already used for a different request.
refusals.remedy: Start the action again, so a new key is used.

refusals.means: A repeat of a request whose answer showed a secret once: the secret isn't kept, so it can't be shown again.
refusals.remedy: If the secret was lost, issue a new one.

refusals.means: Your sign-in identity is still being set up.
refusals.remedy: Wait a moment and try again; it works once the set-up has finished.

refusals.means: Something went wrong inside INSYS, not with what you entered.
refusals.remedy: Try again; if it repeats, report it to support with the reference.

refusals.means: The record isn't in a state that allows this action: it has already moved on, or hasn't reached the step yet.
refusals.remedy: Open the record again to see its current status, and take the action that status allows.

refusals.means: The customer, intermediary or provider to link the user to isn't in force, or the intermediary isn't active and licensed.
refusals.remedy: Check the record to link to, and that it's in force.

refusals.means: You made or requested this, and the same person can't also approve it.
refusals.remedy: Ask another person with approval authority to decide it.

refusals.means: This role is privileged and needs the user to be enrolled for a second factor.
refusals.remedy: Enrol the user for a second factor, then assign the role.

refusals.means: No role assignments fall in the scope of this access review.
refusals.remedy: Widen the review's scope, or no review is needed.

refusals.means: The record wasn't found, or you aren't allowed to see it.
refusals.remedy: Check the reference. If you should be able to see it, ask your administrator about your access.

refusals.means: The service is starting up.
refusals.remedy: Try again shortly.

refusals.means: The platform operator's organisation holds no business records, so this action isn't available there.
refusals.remedy: Use an insurer's tenant for business work.

refusals.means: The record is outside the products or organisation units your role covers.
refusals.remedy: Ask a colleague whose scope covers it, or ask your administrator to widen your scope.

refusals.means: This portal needs a second factor, and your sign-in didn't include one.
refusals.remedy: Sign in again and complete the one-time code step.

refusals.means: The step waits on a review of the customer's details.
refusals.remedy: Nothing to do now; the step becomes available once the review is finished.

refusals.means: The record changed after you opened it, so your change wasn't saved.
refusals.remedy: Open the record again to see the latest version, then make your change on it.

refusals.means: The change needs the version of the record it's made on.
refusals.remedy: Open the record again and make the change from there.

refusals.means: The process has already ended or hasn't started, so it can't move on.
refusals.remedy: Open the record to see where it stands.

refusals.means: Too many requests in a short time.
refusals.remedy: Wait a moment and try again.

refusals.means: The review can't be completed while some of its items are neither confirmed nor revoked.
refusals.remedy: Confirm or revoke each remaining item, then complete the review.

refusals.means: The user already holds this role, or its assignment is waiting for approval.
refusals.remedy: Nothing to do, or wait for the pending approval.

refusals.means: The user doesn't hold this role.
refusals.remedy: Check the user's roles in force.

refusals.means: The role has no version in force.
refusals.remedy: Choose a role in force, or ask your administrator to put it in force first.

refusals.means: The role would hold two duties your organisation keeps apart, such as preparing and releasing the same payment, or would give a user holding it both through their other roles.
refusals.remedy: Grant the function to a different role, or end the role's conflicting function first.

refusals.means: This segregation-of-duties rule is part of the platform's baseline, which every organisation keeps in force as a block.
refusals.remedy: Leave the rule as a block with no end date; you can add rules of your own on other pairs of functions.

refusals.means: The role would give the user two duties your organisation keeps apart, such as preparing and releasing the same payment.
refusals.remedy: Give the role to someone else, or remove the conflicting role first.

refusals.means: Your roles give you two duties your organisation keeps apart, such as preparing and releasing the same payment, so you can't do the release or verification part.
refusals.remedy: Ask another person to do it, or ask your administrator to end one of the conflicting roles.

refusals.means: A setup change set is abandoned only while the organisation is being onboarded, and this one is live.
refusals.remedy: Correct a live organisation's configuration through ordinary changes, one table at a time.

refusals.means: Part of what this statement carries forward is on a later statement that is still awaiting approval or payment.
refusals.remedy: Wait until that statement is approved and paid, or rejected, then ask again.

refusals.means: This code already has a version in progress.
refusals.remedy: Finish or discard that version first.

refusals.means: Some lines of the import have errors, so nothing was saved.
refusals.remedy: Correct the lines listed and import again.

refusals.means: Only the person who created the draft can change it, so who made the change stays known.
refusals.remedy: Ask the draft's maker to change it, or start your own draft once it's finished.

refusals.means: The new version would start before the version now in force starts.
refusals.remedy: Set the start date after the start of the version in force.

refusals.means: The change is at a scope this table doesn't allow: some tables hold only an organisation's own rows, others only platform-wide rows.
refusals.remedy: Make the change at the table's own scope; platform-wide rows are changed by the platform's administrators.

refusals.means: Static data changes are made by identified people, for maker-checker.
refusals.remedy: Make the change signed in as yourself.

refusals.means: The user already has a portal link pending or in effect.
refusals.remedy: Use the existing link, or end it before making another.

refusals.means: The user has no portal link pending or in effect.
refusals.remedy: Make the link first.

refusals.means: This task closes by itself when its record does what the task asks; it can't be closed by hand.
refusals.remedy: Complete the work on the record; the task then closes.

refusals.means: The request didn't say which organisation it's for.
refusals.remedy: Sign in again; if it persists, report it to support with the reference.

refusals.means: The organisation already has users, so first administrators can't be set up again.
refusals.remedy: Ask for an additional administrator instead.

refusals.means: Your organisation is still being set up, so business actions aren't open yet.
refusals.remedy: Only set-up and configuration work is possible until the organisation is activated.

refusals.means: First administrators are set up only while the organisation is being onboarded.
refusals.remedy: For a live organisation, ask for an additional administrator instead.

refusals.means: The condition for moving the process to that step doesn't hold yet.
refusals.remedy: Complete what the step needs first, then try again.

refusals.means: The process doesn't allow a move from its current step to the one asked for.
refusals.remedy: Open the record to see its current step and the moves it allows.

refusals.means: The reference you typed isn't the one this step acts on, so nothing was done.
refusals.remedy: Copy the reference shown on the record exactly, then send the step again.

refusals.means: You aren't signed in, or your sign-in has expired.
refusals.remedy: Sign in again.

refusals.means: The username is already in use.
refusals.remedy: Choose another username.

refusals.means: The request is missing a required value, or a value isn't in the form, range or state the action allows.
refusals.remedy: Correct what the refusal points to, on the form or in its message, and send it again.

refusals.means: The process definition isn't valid, so the process can't be run.
refusals.remedy: Ask the person who maintains process definitions to correct it.
